        token_data = token_response.json()

        # Create or update Facebook account

docs.title: Data Retrieval
docs.text:
Fetch YouTube data using:

def fetch_youtube_data(token):
    """Fetch YouTube data using the platform's API"""
    api_url = 'https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/channels'
    params = {
        'part': 'snippet,contentDetails,statistics',
        'mine': 'true',
        'access_token': token
    }

    # Get the channel info first
    response = requests.get(api_url, params=params)
    if response.status_code != 200:
        return None

    channel_data = response.json()
    channel_id = channel_data['items'][0]['id']

    # Now get videos for this channel
    videos_url = 'https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/search'
    videos_params = {
        'part': 'snippet',
        'channelId': channel_id,
        'maxResults': 50,
        'order': 'date',
        'access_token': token
    }

    videos_response = requests.get(videos_url, params=videos_params)
    if videos_response.status_code != 200:
        return channel_data

    # Combine the data
    return {
        'channel': channel_data,
        'videos': videos_response.json()
    }

docs.title: Authorization Flow
docs.text:
Implement these views for LinkedIn OAuth:

@login_required
def linkedinAuthorize(request):
    """Initiate LinkedIn OAuth flow"""
    csrf_token = get_token(request)
    request.session['linkedin_csrf_token'] = csrf_token

    authorization_url = (
        f"https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization?"
        f"client_id={LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID}&"
        f"redirect_uri={settings.LINKEDIN_REDIRECT_URI}&"
        f"scope=r_liteprofile%20r_emailaddress%20w_member_social&"
        f"response_type=code&"
        f"state={csrf_token}"
    )
    return redirect(authorization_url)

@login_required
def linkedinCallback(request):
    """Handle LinkedIn OAuth callback"""
    code = request.GET.get('code')
    state = request.GET.get('state')
    stored_state = request.session.get('linkedin_csrf_token')

    if not code or not constant_time_compare(state, stored_state):
        messages.error(request, "Invalid authorization request")
        return redirect('profile_management:profile', username=request.user.username)

    try:
        # Exchange code for access token
        token_response = requests.post('https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken', data={
            'grant_type': 'authorization_code',
            'code': code,
            'redirect_uri': settings.LINKEDIN_REDIRECT_URI,
            'client_id': LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID,
            'client_secret': LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET
        })

        if token_response.status_code != 200:
            raise Exception("Failed to obtain access token")

        token_data = token_response.json()

        # Create or update LinkedIn account
        account = create_social_media_account(request.user, 'linkedin', token_data)
        messages.success(request, "LinkedIn account connected successfully")

    except Exception as e:
        messages.error(request, f"Failed to connect LinkedIn account: {str(e)}")

    return redirect('profile_management:profile', username=request.user.username)

docs.title: Data Retrieval
docs.text:
Fetch LinkedIn data using:

def fetch_linkedin_data(token):
    """Fetch LinkedIn data using the platform's API"""
    headers = {
        'Authorization': f"Bearer {token}",
        'cache-control': 'no-cache',
        'X-Restli-Protocol-Version': '2.0.0'
    }

    # Get basic profile information
    profile_response = requests.get('https://api.linkedin.com/v2/me', headers=headers)
    if profile_response.status_code != 200:
        return None

    profile_data = profile_response.json()

    # Get email address
    email_response = requests.get('https://api.linkedin.com/v2/emailAddress?q=members&projection=(elements*(handle~))', headers=headers)
    if email_response.status_code == 200:
        email_data = email_response.json()
        profile_data['email'] = email_data

    return profile_data

docs.title: Authorization Flow
docs.text:
Implement these views for X OAuth:

@login_required
def twitterAuthorize(request):
    """Initiate X (Twitter) OAuth flow"""
    csrf_token = get_token(request)
    request.session['twitter_csrf_token'] = csrf_token

    authorization_url = (
        f"https://twitter.com/i/oauth2/authorize?"
        f"client_id={TWITTER_CLIENT_ID}&"
        f"redirect_uri={settings.TWITTER_REDIRECT_URI}&"
        f"scope=tweet.read%20users.read%20offline.access&"
        f"response_type=code&"
        f"state={csrf_token}"
    )
    return redirect(authorization_url)

@login_required
def twitterCallback(request):
    """Handle X (Twitter) OAuth callback"""
    code = request.GET.get('code')
    state = request.GET.get('state')
    stored_state = request.session.get('twitter_csrf_token')

    if not code or not constant_time_compare(state, stored_state):
        messages.error(request, "Invalid authorization request")
        return redirect('profile_management:profile', username=request.user.username)

    try:
        # Convert client ID and secret to Base64 for Basic Auth
        auth_str = f"{TWITTER_CLIENT_ID}:{TWITTER_CLIENT_SECRET}"
        auth_bytes = auth_str.encode('ascii')
        auth_b64 = base64.b64encode(auth_bytes).decode('ascii')

        # Exchange code for access token
        token_response = requests.post(
            'https://api.twitter.com/2/oauth2/token',
            headers={
                'Authorization': f'Basic {auth_b64}',
                'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
            },
            data={
                'code': code,
                'grant_type': 'authorization_code',
                'client_id': TWITTER_CLIENT_ID,
                'redirect_uri': settings.TWITTER_REDIRECT_URI,
                'code_verifier': 'challenge'  # Should be generated and stored properly
            }
        )

        if token_response.status_code != 200:
            raise Exception("Failed to obtain access token")

        token_data = token_response.json()

        # Create or update X (Twitter) account
        account = create_social_media_account(request.user, 'x', token_data)
        messages.success(request, "X (Twitter) account connected successfully")

    except Exception as e:
        messages.error(request, f"Failed to connect X (Twitter) account: {str(e)}")

    return redirect('profile_management:profile', username=request.user.username)

docs.title: Data Retrieval
docs.text:
Fetch X (Twitter) data using:

def fetch_twitter_data(token):
    """Fetch X (Twitter) data using the platform's API"""
    headers = {
        'Authorization': f"Bearer {token}",
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }

    # Get user information
    me_response = requests.get('https://api.twitter.com/2/users/me?user.fields=description,profile_image_url,public_metrics', headers=headers)
    if me_response.status_code != 200:
        return None

    user_data = me_response.json()
    user_id = user_data['data']['id']

    # Get recent tweets
    tweets_response = requests.get(
        f'https://api.twitter.com/2/users/{user_id}/tweets?max_results=100&tweet.fields=created_at,public_metrics',
        headers=headers
    )

    if tweets_response.status_code == 200:
        user_data['tweets'] = tweets_response.json()

    return user_data

        f"redirect_uri={settings.TIKTOK_REDIRECT_URI}&"
        f"scope=user.info.basic,video.list&"
        f"response_type=code&"

@login_required
def tiktokCallback(request):
    """Handle TikTok OAuth callback"""
    code = request.GET.get('code')
    state = request.GET.get('state')
    stored_state = request.session.get('tiktok_csrf_token')

    if not code or not constant_time_compare(state, stored_state):
        messages.error(request, "Invalid authorization request")
        return redirect('profile_management:profile', username=request.user.username)

    try:
        # Exchange code for access token
        token_response = requests.post(
            'https://open-api.tiktok.com/oauth/access_token/',
            data={
                'client_key': TIKTOK_CLIENT_KEY,
                'client_secret': TIKTOK_CLIENT_SECRET,
                'code': code,
                'grant_type': 'authorization_code',
                'redirect_uri': settings.TIKTOK_REDIRECT_URI
            }
        )

        if token_response.status_code != 200:
            raise Exception("Failed to obtain access token")

        token_data = token_response.json()
        if token_data.get('message') != 'success':
            raise Exception(f"TikTok error: {token_data.get('data', {})}")

        # Create or update TikTok account
        account = create_social_media_account(request.user, 'tiktok', token_data.get('data', {}))
        messages.success(request, "TikTok account connected successfully")

    except Exception as e:
        messages.error(request, f"Failed to connect TikTok account: {str(e)}")

    return redirect('profile_management:profile', username=request.user.username)

docs.text:
Fetch TikTok data using:

def fetch_tiktok_data(token):
    """Fetch TikTok data using the platform's API"""
    # Get user info
    user_info_response = requests.get(
        'https://open-api.tiktok.com/user/info/',
        params={
            'access_token': token,
            'fields': 'open_id,union_id,avatar_url,display_name,bio_description,profile_deep_link'
        }
    )

    if user_info_response.status_code != 200:
        return None

    user_data = user_info_response.json()
    if user_data.get('message') != 'success':
        return None

    # Get videos
    videos_response = requests.get(
        'https://open-api.tiktok.com/video/list/',
        params={
            'access_token': token,
            'fields': 'id,create_time,cover_image_url,share_url,video_description,duration,height,width,title,embed_html,like_count,comment_count,share_count,view_count'
        }
    )

    if videos_response.status_code == 200:
        videos_data = videos_response.json()
        if videos_data.get('message') == 'success':
            user_data['videos'] = videos_data.get('data', {})

    return user_data.get('data', {})

docs.title: Creating/Updating Social Media Accounts
docs.text:
def create_social_media_account(user, platform, token_data):
    """Helper function to create or update social media account"""
    account, created = SocialMediaAccount.objects.get_or_create(
        user=user,
        platform=platform,
        defaults={
            'token': token_data.get('access_token'),
            'token_type': token_data.get('token_type', 'bearer'),
            'expires': timezone.now() + timedelta(seconds=token_data.get('expires_in', 3600)),
            'is_linked': True
        }
    )

    if not created:
        account.token = token_data.get('access_token')
        account.token_type = token_data.get('token_type', 'bearer')
        account.expires = timezone.now() + timedelta(seconds=token_data.get('expires_in', 3600))
        account.is_linked = True
        account.save()

    return account

docs.title: Disconnecting Platforms
docs.text:
@login_required
def disconnectPlatform(request, platform):
    """Disconnect a social media platform"""
    try:
        account = SocialMediaAccount.objects.get(user=request.user, platform=platform)
        account.is_linked = False
        account.save()
        messages.success(request, f"{platform.title()} account disconnected successfully")
    except SocialMediaAccount.DoesNotExist:
        messages.error(request, f"No {platform.title()} account found")

    return redirect('profile_management:profile', username=request.user.username)

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
When implementing social media integrations, follow these security best practices:

  1. Secure Storage of Credentials:
  2. Never hardcode client IDs and secrets in your code
  3. Use environment variables or a secure secrets management system

  4. If using Django, store secrets in secrets.py and exclude it from version control

  5. OAuth State Parameter:

  6. Always use the state parameter to prevent CSRF attacks

  7. Verify the state parameter in callback functions

  8. Token Storage:

  9. Encrypt access tokens before storing them in the database
  10. Set appropriate expiration times for sessions and tokens

  11. Implement token refresh mechanisms for long-lived access

  12. Error Handling:

  13. Implement comprehensive error handling
  14. Provide clear error messages to users

  15. Log errors for debugging, but do not expose sensitive information

  16. Scope Limitations:

  17. Request only the permissions your application needs
  18. Be transparent with users about what permissions you're requesting
  19. Provide a clear privacy policy explaining how you use their data

docs.title: Extending to New Platforms
docs.text:
To add support for a new social media platform:

  1. Research the platform's OAuth implementation and API documentation
  2. Register a developer application on the platform
  3. Add the platform to the PLATFORMS choices in the SocialMediaAccount model: 
    PLATFORMS = {
    # Existing platforms
    ('new_platform', 'New Platform'),
}
  4. Create authorization and callback views for the platform
  5. Implement a data retrieval function
  6. Update templates to support the new platform
  7. Test the integration thoroughly

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common integration issues and their solutions:

docs.title: OAuth Redirects Not Working
docs.text:
• Check that the redirect URI exactly matches what's registered on the platform
  • Ensure HTTPS is used in production
  • Verify that the client ID and secret are correct

docs.title: Access Token Expiration
docs.text:
• Implement token refresh mechanisms
  • Store token expiration time and check before making API calls
  • Handle re-authorization gracefully if tokens expire

docs.title: API Rate Limiting
docs.text:
• Implement rate limiting detection and backoff strategies
  • Cache API responses where appropriate
  • Monitor usage to stay within platform limits

docs.title: Data Retrieval Issues
docs.text:
• Platform API changes: Keep up with platform API version changes
  • Handle changes to response formats gracefully
  • Implement robust error handling for API requests

Remember to regularly review platform documentation, as APIs and authentication methods may change over time. Stay informed about security best practices and platform policy changes to maintain compliant and secure integrations.

docs.title: Sign Up
docs.text:
• Users are required to provide a username, email address and a password to sign up.
  • Password Requirements: At least 8 characters, containing one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.
  • Upon submission, the system validates the provided data (ensuring the email format is correct, the password meets security standards, and no existing account uses the same email and username).
  • A verification link is sent to the provided email to confirm the account.
  • Once validated, a new User and associated UserProfile are created in the database using Django's User and UserProfile models.

docs.title: Sign In
docs.text:
• Users must provide the email and password they registered with.
  • The system uses Django's built-in authentication methods to verify the credentials. If valid, the user is logged in, and a session is created.
  • Upon successful authentication, the user is redirected to their profile dashboard.
  • If the credentials are incorrect, an error message is displayed, and the user is prompted to try again upto 3 times everytime.

docs.title: Sign Out
docs.text:
• When users sign out, Django invalidates their session and clears any authentication tokens.
  • This ensures they cannot access restricted pages unless they log in again.

docs.title: Complete Profile
docs.text:
• After account creation, users are prompted to complete their profile. They can upload a profile picture, add a bio, and connect social media accounts.
  • Uploaded images are handled via Django’s ImageField and stored in the designated media directory. A default profile picture is used if none is uploaded.
  • User-specific QR codes are also generated and stored for future sharing.

docs.title: Update Profile
docs.text:
• Users can update personal information, such as their full name, bio, profile picture, and social media connections, via their profile settings.
  • The system handles file uploads using Django's form validation and saves updated profile data to the UserProfile model.

docs.title: Connect Accounts
docs.text:
• Users can link their social media accounts (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, etc.) by clicking on the respective social media icons in the profile settings.
  • This action redirects the user to the corresponding OAuth authorization page, where they must approve access.
  • Upon successful authorization, a token is stored in the database (models like Facebook, Instagram, etc.) for future API interactions.

docs.title: Sync Data
docs.text:
• After authentication, the system uses the OAuth tokens to fetch relevant data from the connected accounts.
  • Data from social media platforms, such as user posts and metadata, is stored in data fields (as JSON) in their respective models (e.g., Facebook, Instagram).

docs.title: Create Post
docs.text:
• Users can create a new post via a form where they select the content type: text, image, or video.
  • If an image or video is selected, the file is uploaded using Django's FileField, which ensures appropriate file storage and access.
  • The post is stored in the Post model, which includes fields for the content type, media files, and any associated metadata (timestamps, content description).

docs.title: Update Post
docs.text:
• Users can edit existing posts. When editing a post, they can change the content type (switch from text to image, for example), upload a new media file, or update the description.
  • The updated_at field in the Post model is automatically updated whenever a post is modified.

docs.title: Delete Post
docs.text: • Users can delete posts by calling a specific URL with the post’s primary key (pk). Once confirmed, the system removes the post from the database and deletes associated media files from the server storage.

docs.title: Content Sharing Across Social Media Platforms
docs.text:
After a user creates, updates, or deletes a post (whether it’s a text, image, or video), the system provides the option to synchronize these changes across any linked social media accounts (such as Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, etc.). Here’s how the process works:

  • The system retrieves the necessary authentication tokens from the respective social media models (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn), which were stored when the user linked their accounts.
  • Using these tokens, the system interacts with the APIs of the respective platforms to carry out the desired action (create, update, or delete) on the user’s behalf.
  • For each action, the system logs the status of the process (successful or failed) and handles any errors that occur, such as expired tokens, invalid post IDs, or platform-specific restrictions. In such cases, the user is notified.

docs.title: Synchronization
docs.text:
For each action (create, update, or delete), the system maintains synchronization with the external platforms:

  • The lastsync field in the corresponding social media models (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, etc.) is updated to track the most recent interaction with the respective platform.
  • The ConnectedAccounts model tracks the status of linked accounts, providing feedback to users about whether their content has been successfully posted, updated, or deleted across the connected platforms.

docs.title: Welcome to SLID
docs.text:
SLID is your unified digital identity platform, bringing together all your social media accounts in one clean, user-friendly interface. With SLID, you can manage multiple social media platforms, interact with your connections, and navigate your digital presence seamlessly using our AI-powered tools.

This manual will guide you through all the features of SLID and help you make the most of your digital identity management.

docs.title: What is SLID?
docs.text:
SLID (Social Linked Identity Dashboard) is a platform that integrates your social media and online accounts into one user-friendly interface. It serves as your digital ID, centralizing and unifying your digital presence across platforms.

Key Features: - Unified social media experience - AI-powered data navigation - Digital identity management - Cross-platform integration - Secure authentication

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text: SLID is a web-based application that works on: - Any modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) - Desktop, tablet, and mobile devices

docs.title: Creating a New Account
docs.text:
1. Visit SLID website
  2. Click the "Sign Up" button
  3. Enter your desired username, email address, and password
  4. Click "Create Account"
  5. Verify your email address by clicking the link sent to your email
  6. Accept the terms and conditions

docs.title: Setting Up Your Profile
docs.text:
After signing up, you'll be prompted to complete your profile:

  1. Add your full name
  2. Upload a profile picture
  3. Write a short bio
  4. Set your profile visibility preferences

Your profile completeness will be displayed as a percentage. A complete profile enhances your SLID experience and helps others find and connect with you.

docs.title: Supported Platforms
docs.text: SLID currently supports these social media platforms: - Facebook - Instagram - X (formerly Twitter)

docs.title: How to Connect an Account
docs.text:
1. From your dashboard, click on "Connected Accounts"
  2. Select the platform you want to connect
  3. Click "Connect"
  4. You'll be redirected to the platform's authorization page
  5. Log in to the platform if needed
  6. Grant SLID permission to access your account
  7. You'll be redirected back to SLID once connected

docs.title: Permissions and Privacy
docs.text:
When connecting accounts, SLID will request only the permissions it needs to function: - Basic profile information - Content access - Post creation capabilities (optional)

SLID does not: - Post without your permission - Access private messages - Store your platform passwords

You can review and modify these permissions at any time.

docs.title: Dashboard Overview
docs.text:
Your SLID dashboard is organized into these main sections:

Profile Summary - Your profile completeness score - Quick statistics from connected accounts - Recent activity

Connected Accounts - List of all connected social platforms - Connection status for each platform - Quick actions for each platform

Content Feed - Aggregated content from your accounts - Content creation tools - Filter options

Connections - People you're connected with on SLID - Connection recommendations - Connection management

docs.title: Personalization Options
docs.text:
Customize your SLID experience:

  1. Click on "Settings" in the top-right menu
  2. Under "Appearance," choose your theme preference
  3. Under "Dashboard," arrange widgets as you prefer
  4. Set your default view for when you log in

docs.title: Viewing Your Content

  1. Go to the "Content" tab
  2. Use filters to sort by:
  3. Platform
  4. Date
  5. Content type (images, videos, text)

docs.title: Creating Content

  2. Choose content type (text, image, video)
  3. Upload media or write your text
  4. Select which platforms to post to

  3. Compare performance between different platforms

docs.title: What the AI Can Do

  • Answer questions about your social media activity
  • Find specific posts or interactions
  • Identify patterns in your content
  • Make recommendations for improving engagement
  • Help you discover connections across platforms

  2. Type your question in natural language
  3. Press Enter or click "Ask"

Example queries: - "Show me my most popular Instagram posts from last month" - "When did I last interact with Jane on Facebook?" - "Which of my posts mentioned climate change?" - "Find connections I have on both LinkedIn and Twitter"

  • Mention specific platforms when relevant
  • Use names of connections you're asking about
  • Provide context if the AI misunderstands

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Can't Connect a Social Media Account - Check that you're using the correct login credentials - Ensure you're not in private browsing mode - Try disconnecting and reconnecting the account - Verify the platform's servers are online

Content Not Displaying - Check your connection to the platform is still active - Refresh your SLID dashboard - Verify the content still exists on the original platform - Check your internet connection

AI Assistant Not Responding - Refresh the page - Try rephrasing your question - Check if you've reached the daily query limit - Ensure your request is related to your social data

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
If you need assistance:

  1. Check the FAQ section in "Help"
  2. Use the AI assistant for general guidance
  3. Contact support through:
  4. In-app chat (business hours)
  5. Email at support@slid.example.com
  6. Knowledge base at help.slid.example.com

docs.title: Reporting Bugs
docs.text:
If you encounter a bug:

  1. Go to "Settings" > "Help & Support"
  2. Click "Report a Bug"
  3. Describe what happened
  4. Include steps to reproduce the issue
  5. Add screenshots if possible

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
SLID empowers you to take control of your digital identity across multiple platforms. As you connect more accounts and explore the features, you'll discover new ways to streamline your social media management and enhance your online presence.

We're constantly improving SLID based on user feedback. Feel free to share your experiences and suggestions through the feedback form in the app.

Thank you for choosing SLID as your digital identity platform!
